My dog, Biscuit, has always been pretty calm, which is exactly why what happened last weekend was such a surprise to everyone in the house.
I was bringing in groceries, and I left the front door open for like ten seconds while I grabbed another bag from the trunk of the car.
That was apparently all the time Biscuit needed.
By the time I turned around, he was already halfway down the street, running like he'd just been released from prison after a long sentence.
I dropped the groceries right there on the porch and took off after him, still in my socks, not even thinking about shoes.
He ran straight toward the park a few blocks away, and I chased him the whole way there, yelling his name over and over, which did absolutely nothing at all.
Dogs, I've learned, do not care about their name when they're having the best day of their entire life.
At the park, things got worse.

He spotted a squirrel and just completely lost his mind, chasing it in circles around a tree while I tried to catch up, gasping for air and definitely regretting every single workout I'd ever skipped this year.
A woman nearby saw the whole thing happening and started laughing, then kindly offered to help me out.
She had a bag of treats in her purse, because apparently she always carries dog treats around, just in case something like this happens.
She crouched down, shook the bag, and Biscuit stopped dead in his tracks like someone had hit pause on him.
He walked right over to her, completely forgetting about the squirrel, the park, and me, tail wagging like she was the most important person he'd ever met.
I finally caught up, grabbed his collar, and just stood there catching my breath while this total stranger fed my dog a treat like she'd known him his whole life.
A couple of kids nearby had stopped their own game to watch the whole thing, laughing every time Biscuit spun in another circle chasing his own tail out of pure excitement.
Even a guy jogging past slowed down just to see what all the commotion was about.
I thanked her about five times and practically carried Biscuit home after that, just to be extra safe, refusing to let go of his collar the entire way.
When we got back, the groceries were still sitting on the porch exactly where I'd dropped them, and somehow a bag of bread had completely disappeared in all the chaos.
I'm pretty sure I know exactly who took it, and he did not look sorry about it at all, lying by the door looking extremely pleased with himself.
